subject: Vocabulary
description: Latin / French phrases used in English; high-hit SSC PYQ items

questions.stem: What does the Latin phrase 'STATUS QUO' mean?

options.option_text: A new beginning fresh and clean

questions.explanation: STATUS QUO (Latin) = 'the state in which' = the existing state of affairs. 'Maintain status quo' = keep things as they are; don't change. 'Status quo ante' = the previous state (before something happened). Common in legal, diplomatic, political contexts. PYQ-favourite.
questions.subject: Vocabulary

questions.explanation: BONA FIDE = 'in good faith' (Latin). Used to mean genuine, sincere, real. 'A bona fide claim' = genuine claim. 'Bona fide certificate' = genuine school/employment certificate. Antonym: MALA FIDE = bad faith. Other Latin pairs: prima facie (at first sight), de facto (in fact), de jure (in law), in toto (in total), pro rata (proportional), per capita (per head).
questions.subject: Vocabulary

questions.explanation: MODUS OPERANDI (M.O.) = method of operating; way of working. Often used for criminals: 'the burglar's MO was to enter through windows'. Modus vivendi = mode/way of living (esp. compromise allowing two parties to coexist). Modus tollens / modus ponens = logical inference rules.
questions.subject: Vocabulary

questions.explanation: COUP D'ÉTAT (lit. 'stroke of state') — sudden, illegal overthrow of government, often by military. Commonly shortened to 'COUP'. Examples: Napoleon's coup (1799); various Latin America + Africa coups in 20th c.; Myanmar coup (2021). Other French phrases in English: COUP DE GRACE (= 'mercy stroke', the killing blow); BON VOYAGE (good journey); CARTE BLANCHE (full freedom); FAUX PAS (false step / social blunder); RENDEZVOUS (meeting); DEJA VU (already seen); NOUVEAU RICHE (newly rich); SAVOIR FAIRE (know how).
questions.subject: Vocabulary

questions.explanation: IN CAMERA = 'in the chamber' (Latin) = privately, in chambers; closed to public. Used in legal contexts: 'the case was heard in camera' = closed-door hearing (often for sensitive matters: rape, child abuse, national security). NOT related to photography 'camera' (although same Latin root — 'chamber'). PYQ-favourite legal Latin.
questions.subject: Vocabulary

questions.explanation: AB INITIO = 'from the beginning' (Latin). 'The contract was void ab initio' = invalid from the very start. 'I'll start ab initio' = from scratch. Other 'ab' phrases: AB OVO = 'from the egg' (from origin, similar meaning); AB EXTRA = from outside.

questions.stem: What does 'PRIMA FACIE' (Latin) mean in legal context?
questions.explanation: PRIMA FACIE = 'on the face of it' / 'at first sight'. Suggests apparent truth, not yet proven. 'A prima facie case' = enough evidence to proceed; not yet proof. Compare with 'beyond reasonable doubt' (criminal — much higher standard) + 'preponderance of evidence' (civil — > 50%). Also: prima donna = leading female opera singer; prima ballerina; primary; primer.
